names.context: Finally, in terms of its science activities Curiosity is examining a wind-formed, long, narrow, large ripple which has been named “Chocolatal.” Further examination will help determine if this feature could be classified as a “transverse aeolian ridge” or TAR.

names.name: Peace River
names.context: ChemCam was able to analyze the chemistry of another nearby bedrock target, “Peace River,” and use its imaging and passive spectroscopic capabilities to look at the new drill hole and surrounding tailings.

names.name: Nazca
names.context: I was on planning Friday as Geology and Mineralogy Science Theme Lead when we received our close-up views of the neighbor block from the post-drive imaging and our team was happy to see that it was jam-packed with the “disc- and needle-” shaped lumps, just like “Chiu Chiu.” We quickly gave the science go-ahead to proceed with preparations for drilling at the newly named “Nazca” site.

names.name: Toucan
names.context: Meanwhile, the ChemCam LIBS will conduct a “depth profile” experiment to obtain compositional information from slightly deeper layers within a nearby crystal-form-rich target, “Toucan”.

names.name: Condor
names.context: The third LIBS of the plan will go to “Condor,” a nearby block in which a finely layered texture is exposed.

names.name: Palpala
names.context: Other ChemCam activities this week included a LIBS investigation of “Palpala,” which is a dark pebble.

names.name: Puna
names.context: Another such pebble was the target “Puna” identified in Friday’s planning.

names.name: Llama
names.context: ChemCam LIBS on the target “Llama” is to get another depth profile to check whether our observations in the first such depth profile are consistently observed or whether they vary between locations.

names.name: Pacaya
